paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: faith is trusting God about what you can't see yet. The writer says it's "the assurance of what we hope for and the certainty of what we do not see." (Hebrews 11:1) And it matters, because "without faith it is impossible to please God." (Hebrews 11:6) That's not a pile of rules, that's an invitation to trust Him.

Look at who the writer lines up. Noah is warned about things not yet seen, and he builds. (Hebrews 11:7) Abraham goes without knowing where he's going, and Sarah "considered Him faithful who had promised." (Hebrews 11:8, 11) Not one of them had the whole picture, and I know that feeling, because I couldn't see past the back of a drawer for YEARS. They leaned on God's faithfulness, and that's the part that holds you up when the map runs out.

These people "died in faith, without having received the things they were promised," yet they kept longing for "a better country, a heavenly one." (Hebrews 11:13, 16) So when your waiting gets long, you're in good company. And listen to this: "God is not ashamed to be called their God, for He has prepared a city for them." (Hebrews 11:16) Keep trusting Him, baker, because He's already got your place ready.
